findings.summary: Host enforcement for `loom-pr-merge-gate` is not yet proven by live GitHub readback: branch protection or an active ruleset must require the stable check name, and a real PR-head run must exist before the PR #762 regression class can be closed.

disposition.summary: Collect and record fresh host readback evidence after the workflow is active on a PR.

findings.details: Host enforcement truth lives outside the repo tree; workflow presence and local validation are not enough.

findings.summary: The required check workflow checks out and executes repository code from the PR head. This preserves head binding, but it is a host-trust decision for repositories that accept untrusted external PRs.

disposition.summary: Documented in the PR merge gate contract; repositories can restrict contributors or replace the workflow body with pinned tooling/API-fetched artifacts before requiring the check.

findings.details: The workflow uses read-scoped permissions, but required-check execution of PR-supplied code remains a governance boundary.

findings.summary: The stock workflow currently targets direct PR merges via `pull_request`; repositories that enable GitHub merge queue must explicitly add and validate `merge_group` support.

disposition.summary: Keep merge-queue support out of WI-763 direct PR merge scope unless Loom self-governance enables merge queue.

findings.details: Current live readback showed no active rulesets before this change; merge queue compatibility remains a documented Stage-follow-up decision.
